scope: Fuchs-class subluminal warp-shell G2/G3 forensic follow-up

executive_result.statement: The strongest current evidence supports treating the canonical subluminal Fuchs geometry as a serious positive-energy candidate rather than either validated engineering or refuted physics. Independent reconstruction evidence strengthens the metric/energy-condition side, while a physically realizable constitutive source, formation/control mechanism, stability case, and actuator chain remain unresolved. No gate promotion is authorized by this record.

findings.claim: The original WarpFactory reference implementation is not by itself a complete G2 certificate.
basis: WarpFactory Metrics/utils/TOVconstDensity.m evaluates a closed-form pressure expression using M(end), so the original implementation does not by itself establish a general running-enclosed-mass shell TOV integration.
WarpFactory Analyzer/getEnergyConditions.m defaults to finite observer sampling (100 angular vectors and 10 temporal shells); finite sampling is not equivalent to an analytic all-observer proof.
findings.disposition: Do not use the original numerical pass alone as a full source-admissibility proof.

findings.claim: A corrected independent reconstruction materially strengthens the positive-energy subluminal Fuchs result.
basis: Current Warpax Fuchs construction integrates the TOV equation inward using the running enclosed mass, smooths density/pressure, recomputes cumulative mass, and reconstructs the metric potentials.

Its current construction-verification artifact reports the canonical v=0.02c, R1=10 m, R2=20 m case as Type I on tested grids with positive invariant NEC margins and no detected NEC/WEC/DEC violations in the tested wall samples.
The current observer-robust verification line uses all-causal-direction decision machinery at a point rather than relying only on finite direction sampling.
findings.caveat: The reproduced result is still spatially sampled unless a global spatial enclosure/certificate is supplied; positive metric-derived stress-energy does not identify a realizable material source.
findings.disposition: Keep the Fuchs candidate active in G2; do not promote to G3.

findings.claim: Observer completeness and spatial completeness are separate requirements.
findings.basis: An all-observer test at sampled spacetime points does not prove the condition everywhere in the shell, transition joins, smoothing tails, or boundaries.
findings.disposition: Future G2 certification must close both dimensions independently.

findings.claim: The source problem is better framed as a constitutive-support problem than as a binary exotic-matter question.
basis: A positive-density spherical shell with two vacuum free faces is not generically supportable by nonnegative isotropic pressure alone under the ordinary TOV/free-traction assumptions.

Anisotropic tangential stress can change that conclusion in at least restricted regimes, so the decisive question becomes whether an explicit causal, stable matter/field model can generate the required anisotropy and boundary behavior.
findings.disposition: Require a source Lagrangian/constitutive law or explicit testable surrogate before G2->G3 promotion.

findings.claim: A movable warp shell need not imply reactionless propulsion.
findings.basis: Radiative-steering constructions can change shell momentum by photon emission, explicitly closing momentum through radiation.
findings.disposition: G3 must preserve momentum accounting and must not infer reactionless propulsion from shell motion or geometry language.

findings.claim: Version pinning is mandatory for rapidly evolving preprints and implementations.
findings.basis: Relevant 2026 preprints and implementations have materially changed across revisions, including titles, source assumptions, regularization choices, and conclusions.
findings.disposition: Every swarm finding must record exact preprint version/date and code revision before synthesis.

current_gate_disposition.G1_geometry: Candidate geometry is sufficiently concrete for continued analysis; no engineering implication.

next_decisive_test.purpose: Turn the current literature/code reconciliation into a reproducible G2 adjudication package.
required_work: Reproduce side-by-side the original WarpFactory pressure path, a corrected running-mass TOV path, and the current Warpax Fuchs reconstruction under matched physical parameters.

Separate observer-completeness certification from spatial-completeness certification; use all-observer algebraic tests where available and add spatial interval/enclosure or convergence evidence over the full shell, smoothing tails, joins, and boundaries.
Check free-face radial traction at both shell boundaries and extract the anisotropic principal stresses actually required by the reconstructed metric.
Test conservation and source consistency, and distinguish T=G/(8pi) inversion from an independently specified material/field model.
Pin every paper version and code commit used in the adjudication.
Retain contradictory/null findings; no synthesis by paper count or shared-code vote.
next_decisive_test.success_condition: A machine-readable report that states exactly which G2 requirements are certified, which remain model-dependent, and which fail, without leaking a G2 result into a G3 claim.

interpretation_guardrails: This record is non-authoritative coordination output and conveys no mutation or promotion authority.
Do not summarize the result as 'Fuchs proved a physical warp drive.'
Do not summarize the result as 'Fuchs was refuted.'
Do not convert positive energy-condition margins into a manufacturable-source claim.
Do not convert anomalous force or shell motion into evidence of spacetime curvature without a preregistered metric observable and artifact/momentum closure.
Shared lineage, shared sources, or shared implementations must be disclosed and grouped rather than counted as independent replication.
